Patch policy (Example Widgets Inc., synthetic)
Critical vulnerabilities (CVSS 9.0 and above) must be patched within 72 hours; high (7.0 to 8.9) within 14 days; others within 30 days.
Internet-facing systems are patched first.
If a patch cannot be applied in time, the system owner must file an exception with a compensating control, such as blocking the vulnerable port. Exceptions last at most 90 days.
Compliance last quarter: 88% of critical patches on time (target 95%).
mustCover: critical flaws must be patched within 72 hours

tabs.indepth:
In depth
How fast flaws must be fixed
Critical vulnerabilities must be patched within 72 hours.
[Glossary] CVSS: A 0-to-10 score for how dangerous a security flaw is.
[Glossary] compensating control: Another protection used while a patch is late, such as blocking the affected network port.
Other rules
Some systems are patched earlier than others, and there are exceptions.

tabs.eli5:
ELI5
Computers need fixes
Sometimes programs have holes. People fix them. Some fixes are fast, some are slow, and there are rules and sometimes exceptions, and teams check how they are doing, and there are different scores and some systems are special.

Other rules
Some systems are patched earlier than others. Exceptions are possible. Patching matters because attackers move fast, so it is always best to patch as soon as possible.
